import re
import pytest
from target import url_basename

def old_url_basename(url):
    """Reference implementation using the original regex."""
    m = re.match(r'(?:https?:|)//[^/]+/(?:[^?#]+/)?([^/?#]+)/?(?:[?#]|$)', url)
    if not m:
        return u''
    return m.group(1)

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url",
    [
        # simple paths
        "http://example.com/file",
        "https://example.com/file",
        "http://example.com/file/",
        "https://example.com/file/",
        # with query / fragment
        "http://example.com/file?query=1",
        "https://example.com/file#section",
        "http://example.com/file/?query=1",
        "https://example.com/file/#section",
        # nested paths
        "http://example.com/dir/file",
        "https://example.com/dir/subdir/file",
        "http://example.com/a/b/c/d",
        # trailing slash without basename
        "http://example.com/dir/",
        "https://example.com/dir/subdir/",
        # only domain
        "http://example.com/",
        "https://example.com/",
        "http://example.com",
        "https://example.com",
        # unusual but allowed characters
        "http://example.com/dir.with.dots/file-name_123",
        # double slash in path (should still capture last segment)
        "http://example.com//double//slash/file",
        # scheme omitted (protocol-relative URL)
        "//example.com/file",
        "//example.com/dir/file",
        # non‑http scheme (should not match, return empty)
        "ftp://example.com/file",
        "mailto:user@example.com",
        # path with query but no basename
        "http://example.com/?query=1",
        "https://example.com/#fragment",
        # path containing characters that were previously allowed in the optional segment
        "http://example.com/dir/with/slash/file",
        # path where optional segment contains a slash (old regex allowed, new does not)
        "http://example.com/first/second/third",
    ],
)
def test_url_basename_behaviour(url):
    assert url_basename(url) == old_url_basename(url)
